column1: # GE-T10's yes-or-no set (SMYSL-2.5 OQ-22's owed intent vocabulary, fourth round): ten
# questions, eight verifications asked as a bare yes-or-no question and two guards of other
# intents written with the same verbs, each in the five tier-1 languages, fifty rows, over the
# committed corpus (`../gold/corpus.smy`). Only the front is scored, as on `../sixth/`.
# WHY. `ask --explain` read "Is it true that scurvy is cured by citrus fruit?" and refused "Is
# scurvy cured by citrus fruit?" (SMY-E468): the table reads verification by its openers ("is
# it true that", English `did`/`does`, German `hat`, French `est-ce que`) and not by the shape
# a yes-or-no question takes in each language — a verb first, an inverted subject, a particle.
# THE RULE, DECLARED before a word of this set was written; scored first without it
# (`baseline.txt`), and not changed after a run:
#  27. a yes-or-no question as verification, by the verb that opens it or the inversion that
#      marks it — a LAST-RESORT tier: these rules read a question only when no other rule
#      reads it, so `why is`, `where is`, `pourquoi … -t-il` keep their readings whatever their
#        en  is / are / was / were / has / have / had / do / can / could
#        de  ist / sind / war / waren / wird / werden / wurde / wurden / kann / konnte
#        es  es / son / fue / fueron / se / puede
#      and an infix form only in a question that does not open with a question word:
#        fr  qu' que quel quelle quels quelles qui comment où pourquoi combien quand
#        ru  что кто как где почему зачем когда какой какая какое какие каков сколько откуда
# NOT DECLARED, ON PURPOSE: a Spanish yes-or-no question with no such verb ("¿Probó Jenner su
# vacuna?") is marked only by its question marks, which the table does not see; and French
# `-t-on` is as often an explanation's ("pour quelle raison a-t-on …") as a verification's.
# WHO WROTE THIS. The hand that declared the rule, after declaring it; some rows reach for a
# verb the rule does not list (Spanish `era`, `eran`, French `-t-on`), as a person would.
# Single hand, so no agreement figure.
# Columns as `../gold/questions.tsv`: qid, intent, lang, question.
